title: WinGNN: Dynamic Graph Neural Networks with Random Gradient Aggregation Window

problem.claim: Dynamic GNNs can become oversized and inefficient because temporal encoders add learning parameters.

gap.claim: Previous dynamic GNN models use a fixed temporal term, causing a short-temporal optimum.

contributions.claim: WinGNN models dynamic graphs with a simple GNN, a meta-learning strategy, and random gradient aggregation.
WinGNN passes frame-wise loss gradients between consecutive snapshots to model graph dynamics without temporal encoders.
WinGNN uses a randomized sliding window to aggregate window-aware gradients and update the GNN.

stated_novelty.claim: The framework introduces a novel mechanism of random gradient aggregation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that WinGNN reduces parameter size and improves robustness.
Across six public datasets, the authors report that WinGNN reaches the optimum on twenty-two of twenty-four performance metrics compared with existing baselines.

narrative_sequence.summary: Modeling dynamics in GNNs supports understanding and representation of real-world dynamic graphs.
Temporal encoders add parameters, while fixed temporal terms can produce a short-temporal optimum.
WinGNN combines a simple GNN, meta-learning, and random gradient aggregation to model dynamic graphs.
The method passes gradients across snapshots and aggregates randomized sliding-window gradients without temporal encoders.
Experiments on six public datasets compare WinGNN with existing baselines.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the six datasets, tasks, baselines, or performance metrics.
The abstract does not provide quantitative parameter-size, robustness, or performance results beyond the reported metric count.
